method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file again. That covered title and title.canDo, spec.situation and the new spec.deviation, the Folge (8 lines) and its gist item, and the three inputs: the LS1 chat (9 lines plus Priya's message), the LS2 dialogue (10 lines plus the park website) and the LS3 call (10 lines plus the group chat). It also covered the 5 H3 texts, the strategy card, 8 redemittel, both speaking parts (instructionsDe, situationDe, cards), aiRole, openingLine, 8 hintWords and 15 model turns, and the S2 task (situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte with cues, checklist, model text). Finally it covered the 2 check lines, the 3 micro-outputs, both Aussprache blocks, story.beat and the cliffhanger, every endLine, modelSentence and explanation.de, the 35 u08 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json, and the rule cards rc.koennen, rc.nicht-position-gern and the new a1.2 card rc.nicht-position-gern-2. We solved all 89 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: start gist 1, input 15, structured input 12, pool 33, reserve 15, exam 5 and check 8. There are no proof items. For sentence_building we permuted the tiles, including the Mittelfeld positions of gern, nicht and auch and the V1 questions. For error_correction we tried every correction that keeps the meaning (not only one-edit corrections) and every Duden doublet of the key's words. We ran 90 candidate answers through the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js, and built the dictations exactly as src/components/course-v2/content.js dictationItems builds them. The results are quoted in previousFindings, F02 and F03. We compiled a1.1 into the scratchpad (node scripts/course-v2/compile.mjs a1.1 --out <scratch> --banks-out <scratch>), so nothing was written to the repo. We then ran the server's own normalizeSpeakingTask and buildCoursePartnerPrompt (netlify/functions/_shared/speakingAI.mjs) on the compiled a11-u08-s entry (F01). We walked every German surface with the validator's knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u08, including the surfaces LEX-01 does not read (Folge, modelTurns, hintWords, redemittel, check lines, readAloud, story, model text), and looked up each unknown token in all eight lexicons. Only metalanguage, glossed input words and the cliffhanger's u09 teaser „Kaffee“ remain. We checked exam fidelity against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json and against the rubrics sd1-sp1 and sd1-sp2: h3 = 5 × abc, 3 options, 2 plays, textWords [28–54], tt.telefonansage; sp1 = a keyword sheet on which not every keyword is needed, then a spelled word and a number; sp2 = two rounds, with one question and one answer per candidate per round; s2 = 3 Leitpunkte and about 30 words. Our recounts: H3 41/38/42/38/40, S2 model 31, cliffhanger 20. We read story and cast against u02 (Priya's number and Beruf), u07 (the Thursday cliffhanger), u09 (the café), casts/series.json and casts/a1.json. We verified every deviation claim: sd1.h1 is in u09's Prüfungsfokus, sd1.l2 is in u05's and u06's, lx.verein is a2.1-u07, lx.sonntag is a1.1-u11, and lexiconBlocks lists 35 lemmas. We re-checked every r1 finding against the current files and the rails (scripts/course-v2/rules/*).

verdict: Not exit-ready: 1 BLOCKER, 2 MAJOR, 6 MINOR. The r1 fixes landed well in the unit. Of the 13 findings, 6 are fixed or fixed in the unit (F02, F03, F06, F09, F10, F11), 4 are partly fixed (F01, F04, F08, F13), and 3 are still open with their owners (F05, F07, F12). Every key is right, and every correction prompt now names what to correct. Priya's number matches u02 in both u08 and u12. The story breaks are repaired, the deviation is logged and every claim in it is true, and the German on every model surface is correct. Three things stop exit. (1) F01, BLOCKER, not owned by the unit. The engine defect of u01 r2-F01 is still there: normalizeSpeakingTask drops `parts`, so for a11-u08-s the AI partner gets only the Teil 1 monologue script, with no cards, and the whole session is graded with sd1-sp1. Since the r1-F09 fix, all four can-do proofs point at the speaking task. Three of them (verabreden, zeit-zusagen-absagen, gefallen) are performed only in Teil 2, which the engine neither runs nor scores. (2) F02, MAJOR. The r1-F01 class was closed by listing r1's answers, not by the order rail. The scored Check still rejects „Ich höre Musik nicht gern.“, the very order the unit's own rule card models („Ich koche nicht gern.“). Three practice items reject equally grammatical orders: „Ich höre Musik gern.“, „Gut kann ich schwimmen.“ and „Kann auch Olena kommen?“. (3) F03, MAJOR. The checker grades „gerne“ WRONG wherever „gern“ is typed, the Check included. This is the r1-F03 variant class on the unit's own new core word, and the checker still grades „OK“ WRONG too. The edits in the unit are small: four accepted forms with acceptedWhy (F02), and one reordered line plus one model sentence (F04). Everything else belongs to other owners: the engine (F01), the checker (F03), the rule-smith (F02 and F09) and the lexicon, rule-card and SCHEMA owners (F05–F08). For the level: A1.1 cannot be declared finished before F01 lands. It blocks every A1.1 unit with a multi-Teil speaking task: u01, u04, u05, u06, u08, u09, u10 and u12.

findings.problem: The r1-F01 fix named the category in every correction prompt and added the fronted orders r1 listed, and the ITM-01 naming rail now exists. But the class was closed with a list of ids, not with the order rail r1 asked for, and the unit still marks grammatical orders of the same sentences wrong. One of them is in the scored Check. (1) c05. A bare or definite object may stand before „nicht gern“: „Ich esse Fisch nicht gern.“ is as usual as „Ich esse nicht gern Fisch.“ The rule card models „nicht gern“ at the end of the sentence. The item already accepts „Musik höre ich nicht gern.“, which moves „Musik“ just as far. A learner who follows the card writes exactly „Ich höre Musik nicht gern.“ and gets a red X with no retry. (2) ls2-p07 has the same Mittelfeld order without the negation. (3) ls1-p10. The unit accepts rare fronting with acceptedWhy „grammatisch, aber selten“ („Gern tanze ich nicht.“ in ls2-p05 and „Gern schwimme ich nicht.“ in ls2-p10), but it rejects the same move with „gut“: „Gut kann ich schwimmen.“ This is the weakest instance, and it is still grammatical. (4) ls3-p07. „auch“ may stand before the noun subject with the same meaning: „Kann auch Olena kommen?“ = „Kann Olena auch kommen?“ The u04 exemplar accepted the parallel „Auch die Milch ist billig.“ (u04 r1-F04). orders.mjs can see none of these. It treats gern, nicht and auch as particles that cannot be fronted. In the Mittelfeld it only swaps object pronouns and sentence adverbs. It skips questions. ITM-09 does not run on error_correction at all. §9.4 rates both a defensible second answer that is not accepted and a gate hole that lets the class through as MAJOR. The class is now in its fourth a1.1 round (u01 r1-F16, u04 r5-F01, u08 r1-F01, here), so it stays stop-the-line.

findings.proposedRule: ITM-09 + orders.mjs, extending r1-F01's proposal: (a) run the order computation on the key of every error_correction item whose family is 'order' or whose promptDe names „Position“ or „Wortstellung“, and require each computed order in accepted[] with acceptedWhy; (b) Mittelfeld: a bare or definite object noun may stand on either side of gern, nicht gern and (nicht) gut, except the noun of a verb-noun unit the lexicon lists as a chunk („Rad fahren“); (c) a focus particle (auch, nur) may stand before a full noun-phrase subject; (d) apply (b) and (c) to V1 questions too; (e) Vorfeld: a manner adverb (gut, gern, schnell) can be fronted. findings.problem: „gerne“ is not a spelling slip but the second form of the same word: Duden's headword is „gern, gerne“, and learners hear it every day („Ja, gerne!“). The checker treats the extra „-e“ as a wrong ending and grades every „gerne“ WRONG, with no retry. In this unit that hits the scored Check (c05) and a pool correction (ls2-p10). It will also hit LS1's lex.glossTyped item once the player core builds it from lx.gern: there the learner types the word from its English gloss, and „gerne“ is exactly as right as „gern“. This is the r1-F03 class: a Duden variant graded WRONG („OK“ for „Okay“; u01 r1-F16 „tschüs“). r1 closed the instance by swapping the dictation source, but the rail was not written. So the class has come back on the unit's own new core word, and the checker still grades „OK“ WRONG. It is the third a1.1 occurrence, so it is stop-the-line (§9.4), and every later unit with a typed „gern“ inherits it.
findings.fix: Checker owner (src/lib/lesson/check.js, which decides every answer in the course). Before comparing, fold a closed table of Duden doublets, so that the twin grades like the key: gern/gerne, okay/OK/O. K./o. k., tschüss/tschüs, allein/alleine. Add a test in the checker suite. This also closes r1-F03's class for good. Per CLAUDE.md, do not widen accepted[] in the unit: the rule belongs in the checker. After the fold, c05 with „Ich höre nicht gerne Musik.“ must grade correct. Lexicon owner: record „gerne“ as a variant of lx.gern, so that the glossTyped build accepts it.
findings.proposedRule: A checker test (node --test) plus a course-v2 rail. For every typed item (fill_blank, error_correction, generated lex.glossTyped) whose key contains a token of the doublet table, checkItem on the key with that token swapped for its twin must return CORRECT. exitCheck.note: Exit needs 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, every criterion at 4 or above and at most 5 logged MINOR. F01 is the gate, and the unit does not own it. The E1 server track must read `parts` and score each Teil with its own profile (u01 r2-F01). The defect blocks all eight multi-Teil A1.1 units, so A1.1 cannot be declared finished before the fix lands. F02 needs four accepted forms in the unit plus the order rail. F03 needs a doublet fold in check.js with a test. With those three, A and P return to 4. After the F04 edit in the unit, five owner-held minors remain (F05, F06, F07, F08, F09), which is exactly the limit. Re-review needs no full content round: check P by playing one a11-u08-s session after the engine fix, A by re-running the F02 and F03 candidates through checkItem, and K on the two F04 lines. Class findings for the rule-smith: F01 (the compiled-bank test), F02, F03, F06, F07, F08 and F09. Stop-the-line (§9.4) stays in force for four classes: the order class (fourth a1.1 round), the variant class (third a1.1 occurrence), receptive lemmas that must be produced, and detector noise.

notes: Exemplar classes (u04 r1–r5, u01 r1/r2) that do NOT recur here: sentence-building prompts that do not say Frage or Aussagesatz (u04 r1-F01/F12); dictation sources with `say` (u04 r2-F01; the six sources are plain lines, and the only `say` is in exam text t2); number words rejected in time gaps (u04 r3-F01; ls2-i03 accepts „sieben“ and „neunzehn“, ls3-i03 accepts „zehn“); lex.articlePlural sources without a plural (r3-F03); lex.glossTyped sources on receptive lemmas (r4-F02); exam texts off-band (r1-F10); distractors never heard (r1-F19; all 15 H3 options are heard); protagonists in LS4 texts (r2-F06); a genitive on the speaking instructions (r5-F05; „der Partnerin“ is gone); a bare „Korrigieren Sie:“ that rejects a second correction (r5-F01; ls3-p10 keeps the bare prompt but accepts both V2 corrections, as ITM-01 allows); lexicon examples above the ceiling (r4-F01; LEX-07 passes); factual claims without facts[] (r4-F05).
